key_insight: A longitudinal XGBoost model using non-imaging clinical features can forecast future Alzheimer’s-related cognitive decline before formal diagnosis.
clinical_relevance: If validated further, this approach could support earlier dementia risk stratification using routinely collected clinical data rather than imaging alone.
method: National Alzheimer’s Coordinating Center cohort of 15,727 participants who were cognitively normal or had MCI at baseline
Longitudinal clinical and cognitive features from up to 10 visits were engineered into XGBoost classifiers
Two progression tasks were modeled: CN→MCI and MCI→AD
evidence_signal: On non-imputed data, performance was strong (CN→MCI AUC-ROC 0.9447, PR-AUC 0.8554; MCI→AD AUC-ROC 0.9059, PR-AUC 0.9214), with detectable lead time before diagnosis in a subset of progressors.
watch_item: The results come from retrospective cohort data, so real-world prospective validation and calibration across clinics are still needed before deployment.
paper_title: Forecasting Alzheimer's disease progression using non-imaging clinical features and XGBoost
